q: X-rays are electromagnetic waves like light, but their wavelengths are much ____ than those of light.
e: By the late 1800s light was known to be an electromagnetic wave. X-rays are electromagnetic waves like light, but their wavelengths are much shorter than those of light.

q: Wilhelm Conrad Roentgen discovered X-rays in ____ while experimenting with cathode rays.
e: Cathode rays are electrons in a low-pressure tube. Thomson measured e/m. Wilhelm Conrad Roentgen discovered X-rays in 1895 while experimenting with cathode rays.

q: Because he did not know what the rays were, he called them X-rays, meaning ____ rays.
e: Because he did not know what the rays were, he called them X-rays, meaning unknown rays. The name used here is unknown.

q: Later experiments revealed that X-rays are electromagnetic waves which have a wavelength in the range of ____ to 10 nanometre (nm).
e: By the late 1800s light was known to be an electromagnetic wave. Later experiments revealed that X-rays are electromagnetic waves which have a wavelength in the range of 0.01 to 10 nanometre (nm).

q: They are shorter in wavelength than ultraviolet (UV) rays and longer than ____ rays.
e: They are shorter in wavelength than ultraviolet (UV) rays and longer than gamma rays. Gamma is what this statement is using.

q: X-rays of energy about 0.1 to 10 keV (wavelength 10 to 0.10 nm) are classified as ____ X-rays.
e: X-rays of energy about 0.1 to 10 keV (wavelength 10 to 0.10 nm) are classified as soft X-rays. Soft is what this statement is using.

q: X-rays of energy about 10 to 100keV(wavelength 0.10 to 0.01nm) are classified as ____ X-rays, due to their penetrating abilities.
e: X-rays of energy about 10 to 100keV(wavelength 0.10 to 0.01nm) are classified as hard X-rays, due to their penetrating abilities. Hard is what this statement is using.

q: 1 electron volt (eV) = ____ J is an energy unit used in atomic and nuclear physics.
e: 1 electron volt (eV) = 1.602× 10^-19 J is an energy unit used in atomic and nuclear physics. Leave the relation as 1.602× 10^-19.

q: An X-ray tube consists of a cathode and a target (____).
e: An X-ray tube consists of a cathode and a target (anode). Anode is what this statement is using.

q: A high potential difference (about 10-100 kV) is applied between target and cathode to ____ electrons emitted from the cathode.
e: A high potential difference (about 10-100 kV) is applied between target and cathode to accelerate electrons emitted from the cathode. Accelerate is what this statement is using.

q: X-rays are produced when high-energy electrons strike the target which is made of a high dense material such as ____.
e: X-rays are produced when high-energy electrons strike the target which is made of a high dense material such as tungsten. Tungsten is what this statement is using.

q: X-rays have no charge, cannot be deflected by both electric and ____ fields.
e: Cathode rays go in straight lines, bend in electric or magnetic fields, ionize gas, and make fluorescence. X-rays have no charge, cannot be deflected by both electric and magnetic fields.

q: They travel through vacuum with the speed of ____.
e: They travel through vacuum with the speed of light. Light is what this statement is using.

q: They have high ____ power.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. They have high penetrating power.

q: Hence, thick dense shielding, such as high density concrete or ____ is necessary to protect against X-rays.
e: Density is mass per unit volume, ρ = m/V. Hence, thick dense shielding, such as high density concrete or lead is necessary to protect against X-rays. Lead is what this sentence is naming.

q: Soft tissue(like organs and skin) cannot absorb the X-rays; however high density materials(such as ____) absorb X-rays.
e: Density is mass per unit volume, ρ = m/V. Soft tissue(like organs and skin) cannot absorb the X-rays; however high density materials(such as bone) absorb X-rays. Bone is what this sentence is naming.

q: X-rays can cause ____ by stripping electrons from the atoms and can cause biological effects.
e: X-rays can cause ionization by stripping electrons from the atoms and can cause biological effects. Ionization is what this statement is using.

q: X-rays consist of high energy ____ which are energy packets of electromagnetic wave.
e: A current makes a magnetic field. Soft iron in a solenoid is a temporary magnet; reverse the current and the poles flip. X-rays consist of high energy photons which are energy packets of electromagnetic wave.

q: soft X-rays (low penetrating power) are used to take X-ray photographs of some parts of ____.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. Soft X-rays (low penetrating power) are used to take X-ray photographs of some parts of human body.

q: Hard X-rays (high penetrating power) are used to destroy ____ cells.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. Hard X-rays (high penetrating power) are used to destroy cancer cells.

q: X-rays are used in industries for finding defects in welded joints and metal ____.
e: X-rays are used in industries for finding defects in welded joints and metal castings. Castings is what this statement is using.

q: Since X-rays can exhibit wave nature, they are used to determine the structure of ____.
e: Since X-rays can exhibit wave nature, they are used to determine the structure of crystals. Crystals is what this statement is using.

q: X-rays are also used in security systems to reveal hidden unlawful materials (such as weapons and ____).
e: X-rays are also used in security systems to reveal hidden unlawful materials (such as weapons and drugs). Drugs is what this statement is using.

q: X-rays can be classified as two types: (i) characteristic X-rays (intense sharp lines) and (ii) continuous X-rays (or) ____ X-rays.
e: X-rays can be classified as two types: (i) characteristic X-rays (intense sharp lines) and (ii) continuous X-rays (or) white X-rays. White is what this statement is using.

q: When a high energy electron emitted from the cathode bombard the target material, it may knock an electron in the ____-shell of an atom completely out of its orbit.
e: When a high energy electron emitted from the cathode bombard the target material, it may knock an electron in the inner-shell of an atom completely out of its orbit. Inner is what this statement is using.

q: When outer-shell electrons, having higher energy, fill the vacancy in the inner shell, the energy is released in the form of ____.
e: When outer-shell electrons, having higher energy, fill the vacancy in the inner shell, the energy is released in the form of X-rays. X-rays is what this statement is using.

q: These X-rays are called characteristic X-rays because they have specific energies characteristic of the element used as the ____.
e: These X-rays are called characteristic X-rays because they have specific energies characteristic of the element used as the target. The name used here is target.

q: When an electron striking the target passes through the atoms of the target material, it will suffer a retarding force in the ____ field of the nuclei of the target.
e: When an electron striking the target passes through the atoms of the target material, it will suffer a retarding force in the Coulomb field of the nuclei of the target. Coulomb is what this statement is using.

q: When this occurs, the electron will lose some of its ____ energy and the energy is released in the form of X-rays.
e: When this occurs, the electron will lose some of its kinetic energy and the energy is released in the form of X-rays. Kinetic is what this statement is using.

q: Continuous X-rays are also called ____ radiation (braking radiation) according to the phenomenon they are produced.
e: Conduction needs a material, convection needs a fluid current, radiation needs no medium. Continuous X-rays are also called bremsstrahlung radiation (braking radiation) according to the phenomenon they are produced.
